- When sentiment is consistently negative or near-zero, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecasts by 10–25% in early periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >20% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or use 3-day moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days), model tends to overreact; apply downward bias of 5–15% to avoid overconfidence.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 14-day rolling average as baseline for correction.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model frequently overestimates late-period values; apply exponential decay weighting (e.g., 0.8 decay factor) to recent days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ days of -0.33 or lower), model tends to ignore downward pressure; add 5–10% downward adjustment to forecasted values.
